script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Kia ora, Southern Lights Homestay Network, this is Tom. How can I help?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Hi, good afternoon. I'm starting an English course in Wellington soon, and my college told me to contact you about staying with a host family.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Great, you've come to the right place. Let me open a new request. Can I take your name?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Yes, it's Lena Okafor. That's O-K-A-F-O-R.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Thanks, Lena. And when does your course start?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: There's an orientation day on the first of February, but that's optional. The actual classes begin on the third.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: So you'd want to move in a day or two before the third?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Yes, I'm arriving on the first, so that works.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: And how long will you need the homestay for? Most courses here are twelve weeks.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Mine is twelve weeks, yes, but a friend of mine is coming over in April and we're planning to rent a flat together. So I'll only need the homestay for ten weeks.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Ten weeks, got it. Now, food. Do you have any dietary requirements?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: I eat pretty much everything. Meat, dairy, all that's fine. The only thing is I'm allergic to seafood, so no prawns or fish at all.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: I'll make that very clear to the family. Any other allergies? Some of our hosts have pets.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Dogs are totally fine, I grew up with two. But I can't be around cats. My eyes swell up.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Right, no cats. And how far would you be happy to travel to college each day?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Ideally about thirty minutes. But if the family is really nice, I don't mind up to forty minutes. Not more than that, though.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: OK. Now, there are a few choices to make. First, the room. We have a standard single room with a shared bathroom, a single with its own ensuite bathroom, or a shared twin room, which is cheaper.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: What's the difference in price for the ensuite?

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: It's an extra sixty dollars a week.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Oh, that's quite a lot over ten weeks. And I don't really want to share a bedroom with a stranger. I'll take the standard single with the shared bathroom.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Sensible choice. The weekly fee is three hundred and twenty dollars, and that covers your meals.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: All meals?

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Not quite. Some years ago we did include lunch, but students found it hard to come home in the middle of the day. So now it's breakfast and an evening meal, every day of the week, weekends included.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: That's fine. I can buy lunch near college.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Now, getting from the airport. What time does your flight land?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Er, it's an awful time. Two in the morning.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Ah. Normally hosts can collect students, but there's a charge for that, and to be honest, at two a.m. many hosts would rather not drive. A taxi at that hour is very expensive too. What most students do is take the airport shuttle bus. It runs all night and it'll drop you right at the door.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Oh, the shuttle sounds perfect. Let's do that.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: I'll book it for you. Last thing. To finalise the placement, we need some documents. Have you already sent us a copy of your passport?

script.speaker: Student
script.text: Yes, I uploaded that last week with my application.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Good, I can see it here. Then the only thing missing is your letter of enrolment from the college. We need that by this Friday, otherwise we can't confirm the family.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: And the deposit?

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: Don't worry about the deposit yet. You can pay that once we've matched you with a family. So just the enrolment letter by Friday, please.

script.speaker: Student
script.text: No problem. I'll email it tonight. Thanks so much, Tom.

script.speaker: Adviser
script.text: My pleasure, Lena. You'll hear from us about your family within the next ten days.
